verses.sanskrit:
वैशंपायन उवाच।
              तथा शैलनिपातेन भीषिताः खाण्डवालयाः। दानवा राक्षसा नागास्तरक्ष्वृक्षवनौकसः॥१॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said : The dwellers of the Khandava the Danavas, the Rakshasas, the Nagas the wolves and the bears, the other wild animals, the elephants with their temples rent, the tigers, the lions with manes, hundred of deer and buffaloes, birds and various other creatures, all being frightened by the falling stones and afflicted with anxiety, began to fly in all directions.

verses.sanskrit: द्विपाः प्रभिन्नाः शार्दूलाः सिंहाः केसरिणस्तथा। मृगाश्च महिषाश्चैव शतशः पक्षिणस्तथा॥२॥
समुद्विग्ना विससृपुस्तथान्या भूतजातयः। तं दावं समुदैक्षन्त कृष्णौ चाभ्युद्यतायुधौ॥३॥
verses.english: They saw the fire and also two Krishnas ready with their weapons. Frightened at the fearful sounds, they lost their power of locomotion. Seeing the fire burning in innumerable places and seeing also Krishna with weapons to shoot them down they all set up a terrible roar.
verses.bhavadeepa: प्रभिन्नाः मदच्युताः केसरिण: उत्पन्नकेसराः युवान इत्यर्थः ॥२॥

verses.sanskrit: उत्पातनादशब्देन संत्रासिता इव स्थिताः। ते वनं प्रसमीक्ष्याथ दह्यमानमनेकधा॥४॥
कृष्णमभ्युद्यतास्त्रं च नादं मुमुचुरुल्बणम्। तेन नादेन रौद्रेण नादेन च विभावसोः॥५॥
verses.english: The whole of the firmament resounded with a terrible roar and with also the roar of the fire, as when the clouds roar at the time of the great dissolution.
verses.bhavadeepa: उत्पातनादीः निर्घातादयस्तच्छब्देन संत्रासिते वने इति शेषः । सञ्चारित इति पाठेपि स एवार्थः ॥४॥

verses.sanskrit: ररास गगनं कृत्स्नमुत्पातजलदैरिव। ततः कृष्णो महाबाहुः स्वतेजो भास्वरं महत्॥६॥
verses.english: The mighty-armed Krishna (dark) Keshava hurled at them for their destruction his large, fierce and greatly effulgent discuss.

verses.sanskrit: चक्रं व्यसृजदत्युग्रं तेषां नाशाय केशवः। तेनार्ता जातयः क्षुद्राः सदानवनिशाचराः॥७॥
verses.english: The dwellers of that forest, including the Danavas and the Rakshasas, were struck by that weapon; and being cut into hundred of pieces, they fill into the mouth of Agni (fire).

verses.sanskrit: निकृत्ताः शतशः सर्वा निपेतुरनलं क्षणात्। तत्रादृश्यन्त ते दैत्याः कृष्णचक्रविदारिताः॥८॥
verses.english: Mangled by Krishna's discus, the Daityas were covered with fat and blood; and they looked like the evening clouds.

verses.sanskrit: वसारुधिरसंपृक्ताः सन्ध्यायामिव तोयदाः। पिशाचान्पक्षिणो नागान्पशूंश्चैव सहस्रशः॥९॥
verses.english: O descendant of Bharata, the Vrishni hero Krishna, moving about like Death himself, killed again and again thousands of birds, the Pishachas, the Nagas and other creatures.

verses.sanskrit: निघ्नंश्चरति वार्ष्णेयः कालवत्तत्र भारत। क्षिप्तं क्षिप्तं पुनश्चक्रं कृष्णस्यामित्रघातिनः॥१०॥
verses.english: The discus, being hurled from the hands of Krishna, the slayer of foes killed innumerable creatures, and then it came back again to his hands.

verses.sanskrit: छित्त्वानेकानि सत्वानि पाणिमेति पुनः पुनः। तथा तु निघ्नतस्तस्य पिशाचोरगराक्षसान्॥११॥
verses.english: While he was thus engaged in killing the Pishachas, the Nagas and the Rakshasas, the face and the feature of Krishna, the soul of all creatures, became fearful to look at.

verses.sanskrit: बभूव रूपमत्युग्रं सर्वभूतात्मनस्तदा। समेतानां च सर्वेषां दानवानां च सर्वशः॥१२॥
verses.english: Now the celestial that came to fight and mustered there could not defeat Krishna and Arjuna in battle.

verses.sanskrit: विजेता नाभवत्कश्चित्कृष्णपाण्डवयोर्मृधे। तयोर्बलात्परित्रातुं तं च दावं यदा सुराः॥१३॥
verses.english: When the celestial found that they could not extinguish the fire or protect the forest from the prowess (of Arjuna and Krishna), they retired.

verses.sanskrit: नाशक्नुवञ्शमयितुं तदाऽभूवन्पराङ्मुखाः। शतक्रतुस्तु संप्रेक्ष्य विमुखानमरांस्तथा॥१४॥
verses.english: O king, the deity of one hundred sacrifices (Indra),seeing the immortals retreat (from the battle), became exceedingly glad and much praised Keshava (Krishna) and Arjuna.

verses.sanskrit: बभूव मुदितो राजन्प्रशंसन्केशवार्जुनौ। निवृत्तेष्वथ देवेषु वागुवाचाशरीरिणी॥१५॥
verses.english: When the celestial retreated, an invisible voice thus spoke in a loud and deep voice to the deity of one thousand sacrifices (Indra).

verses.sanskrit: शतक्रतुं समाभाष्य महागम्भीरनिःस्वना। न ते सखा सन्निहितस्तक्षको भुजगोत्तमः॥१६॥
verses.english: "Your friend, that best of the Nagas, Takshaka, has not been slain. Before the fire broke out in the Khandava, he had gone to Kurukshetra.

verses.sanskrit: दाहकाले खाण्डवस्य कुरुक्षेत्रं गतो ह्यसौ। न च शक्यौ युधा जेतुं कथंचिदपि वासव॥१७॥
verses.english: O Vasava, known from what I say that none can ever defeat in battle Vasudeva (Krishna) and Arjuna. They are Nara and Narayana. These two Rishis were formerly heard of in heavens. You will know what is their prowess and energy. They are invincible in battle; these two best of old Rishis are incapable of ever being defeated by any in all the worlds.

verses.sanskrit: वासुदेवार्जुनावेतौ निबोध वचनान्मम। नरनारायणावेतौ पूर्वदेवौ दिवि श्रुतौ॥१८॥
भवानप्यभिजानाति यद्वीर्यौ यत्पराक्रमौ। नैतौ शक्यौ दुराधर्षौ विजेतुमजितौ युधि॥१९॥
अपि सर्वेषु लोकेषु पुराणावृषिसत्तमौ। पूजनीयतमावेतावपि सर्वैः सुरासुरैः॥२०॥
verses.english: They deserve worship from all the celestial, the Asuras, the Yakshas, the Rakshasas, the Gandharvas, the human beings, the Asuras and the Nagas.

verses.sanskrit: यक्षराक्षसगन्धर्वनरकिन्नरपन्नगैः। तस्मादितः सुरैः सार्धं गन्तुमर्हसि वासव॥२१॥
दिष्टं चाप्यनुपश्यैतत्खाण्डवस्य विनाशनम्। इति वाक्यमुपश्रुत्य तथ्यमित्यमरेश्वरः॥२२॥
verses.english: O Vasava, therefore, you should go away from this place with all the celestial. The destruction of the Khandava (forest) has been ordained by fate."

verses.sanskrit: क्रोधामर्षौ समुत्सृज्य संप्रतस्थे दिवं तदा। तं प्रस्थितं महात्मानं समवेक्ष्य दिवौकसः॥२३॥
verses.english: Having ascertained these words to be true, the lord of the immortals Indra gave up his wrath and jealousy and went back to heaven.

verses.sanskrit: सहिताः सेनया राजन्ननुजग्मुः पुरन्दरम्। देवराजं तदा यान्तं सहदेवैरवेक्ष्य तु॥२४॥
verses.english: O king, seeing that illustrious celestial gone away, the dwellers of heaven all followed Indra with their soldiers.

verses.sanskrit: वासुदेवार्जुनौ वीरौ सिंहनादं विनेदतुः। देवराजे गते राजन्प्रहृष्टौ केशवार्जुनौ॥२५॥
verses.english: When those two heroes, Vasudeva and Arjuna, saw the chief of the celestial retreat with all the dwellers of heaven, they set up a leonine roar.

verses.sanskrit: निर्विशङ्कं वनं वीरौ दाहयामासतुस्तदा। स मारुत इवाभ्राणि नाशयित्वाऽर्जुनः सुरान्॥२६॥
verses.english: O king, when Indra had gone away Keshava and Arjuna became exceedingly glad. Those two heroes then fearlessly assisted Agni to consume that forest.

verses.sanskrit: व्यधमच्छरसङ्घातैर्देहिनः खाण्डवालयान्। न च स्म किंचिच्छक्नोति भूतं निश्चरितुं ततः॥२७॥
verses.english: Having scattered the celestial as the wind scatters the cloud, Arjuna killed with the showers of arrows numberless creatures who dwelt in the Khandava.

verses.sanskrit: संच्छिद्यमानमिषुभिरस्यता सव्यसाचिना। नाशक्नुवंश्च भूतानि महान्त्यपि रणेऽर्जुनम्॥२८॥
verses.english: Cut off by Savyasachi's (Arjuna's) arrows, not one among those innumerable creatures could escape (from that burning forest).

verses.sanskrit: निरीक्षितुममोघास्त्रं योद्धुं चापि कुतो रणे। शतं चैकेन विव्याध शतेनैकं पतत्रिणाम्॥२९॥
verses.english: Not to speak of fighting with him none amongst the strongest creatures, who mustered together to fight, could even look at Arjuna with infallible arms. Sometimes piercing one hundred creatures with arrow and sometimes piercing one creature with one hundred arrows.

verses.sanskrit: व्यसवस्तेऽपतन्नग्नौ साक्षात्कालहता इव। न चालभन्त ते शर्म रोधःसु विषमेषु च॥३०॥
verses.english: Arjuna (whirled about one his car). All creatures fell into the mouth of Agni as if struck dead by (Death himself). The creatures found no ease on the banks of the river, or on uneven plains, of in Sakshatas (crematoriums).

verses.sanskrit: पितृदेवनिवासेषु सन्तापश्चाप्यजायत। भूतसङ्घाश्च बहवो दीनाश्चक्रुर्महास्वनम्॥३१॥
verses.english: Everywhere they were afflicted with great heat. Innumerable creatures yelled in pain.

verses.sanskrit: रुरुदुर्वारणाश्चैव तथा मृगतरक्षवः। तेन शब्देन वित्रेसुर्गङ्गोदधिचरा झषाः॥३२॥
verses.english: Elephants, deer and wolves all wept and set up cries of affliction. At the sound the fishes that lived in the waters of the Ganges and the sea.. one

verses.sanskrit: विद्याधरगणाश्चैव ये च तत्र वनौकसः। न त्वर्जुनं महाबाहो नापि कृष्णं जनार्दनम्॥३३॥
verses.english: The various classes of Vidhyadharas, the dwellers of that forest became very much alarmed. O mighty-armed hero, not to speak of fighting with Arjuna and Krishna dark Janardana, none could even look at them.

verses.sanskrit: निरीक्षितुं वै शक्नोति कश्चिद्योद्धुं कुतः पुनः। एकायनगता येऽपि निष्पेतुस्तत्र केचन॥३४॥
राक्षसा दानवा नागा जघ्ने चक्रेण तान्हरिः। ते तु भिन्नशिरोदेहाश्चक्रवेगाद्गतासवः॥३५॥
verses.english: (Krishna) killed with his discus all the Rakshasas, the Nagas and the Danavas who rushed out in crowds.

verses.sanskrit: पेतुरन्ये महाकायाः प्रदीप्ते वसुरेतसि। स मांसरुधिरौधैश्च वसाभिश्चापि तर्पितः॥३६॥
verses.english: Those creatures of huge bodies, their heads and trunks cut off by the swift discus, deprived of their lives, fell down into the burning fire.

verses.sanskrit: उपर्याकाशगो भूत्वा विधूमः समपद्यत। दीप्ताक्षो दीप्तजिह्वश्च संप्रदीप्तमहाननः॥३७॥
verses.english: Being gratified with a large quantity of flesh, blood and fat, the flames rose up to a great height with curling wreath of smoke. Agni with fiery and coppery eyes and with flaming tongue and large mouth.

verses.sanskrit: दीप्तोर्ध्वकेशः पिङ्गाक्षः पिबन्प्राणभृतां वसाम्। तां स कृष्णार्जुनकृतां सुधां प्राप्य हुताशनः॥३८॥
verses.english: Agni with fiery hair on his head, drank with the assistance of Krishna and Arjuna that nectar-like stream of fat. He was filled with great joy and thus being much gratified, he enjoyed much happiness.

verses.sanskrit: बभूव मुदितस्तृप्तः परां निर्वृतिमागतः। तथाऽसुरं मयं नाम तक्षकस्य निवेशनात्॥३९॥
verses.english: Then the slayer of Madhu saw an Asura, named maya suddenly escaping from the abode of Takshaka.

verses.sanskrit: विप्रद्रवन्तं सहसा ददर्श मधुसूदनः। तमग्निः प्रार्थयामास दिधक्षुर्वातसारथिः॥४०॥
शरीरवाञ्जटी भूत्वा नदन्निव बलाहकः। विज्ञाय दानवेन्द्राणां मयं वै शिल्पिनां वरम्॥४१॥
verses.english: Agni, whose charioteer was the wind, immediately assuming a body with (fiery) matted looks on his head and roaring like the clouds, pursued the Asura with the intention of consuming him.

verses.sanskrit: जिघांसुर्वासुदेवस्तं चक्रमुद्यम्य धिष्ठितः। स चक्रमुद्यतं दृष्ट्वा दिधक्षन्तं च पावकम्॥४२॥
verses.english: Seeing the Asura, Vasudeva stood with his weapon upraised, ready to cut him down. Seeing the discus upraised and Agni after him, with the intention of burning him, Maya said "O Arjuna, come soon to me and protect me".

verses.sanskrit: अभिधावार्जुनेत्येवं मयस्त्राहीति चाब्रवीत्। तस्य भीतस्वनं श्रुत्वा मा भैरिति धनंजयः॥४३॥
प्रत्युवाच मयं पार्थो जीवयन्निव भारत। तं न भेतव्यमित्याह मयं पार्थो दयापरः॥४४॥
verses.english: Having heard his frightened voice, Dhananjaya (Arjuna) exclaimed, “Do not fear." O descendant of Bharata, the reply of Partha seemed to give (Maya) his life.

verses.sanskrit: तं पार्थेनाभये दत्ते नमुचेर्भ्रातरं मयम्। न हन्तुमैच्छद्दाशार्हः पावको न ददाह च॥४५॥
verses.english: As the kind Partha said to Maya not to fear, the Dasharha hero (Krishna) did not desire to kill him who was the brother of Namuchi. Agni also did not burn him down.

verses.sanskrit:
वैशंपायन उवाच।
              तद्वनं पावको धीमान्दिनानि दश पञ्च च। ददाह कृष्णपार्थाभ्यां रक्षितः पाकशासनात्॥४६॥
verses.english: Having been protected by Krishna and Partha from the attacks of the chastiser of Paka (Indra), the greatly intelligent Agni burnt the forest for fifteen days.

verses.sanskrit: तस्मिन्वने दह्यमाने षडग्निर्न ददाह च। अश्वसेनं मयं चैव चतुरः शार्ङ्गकांस्तथा॥४७॥
verses.english: In the burning of that forest, he (Agni) speared the lives of only six creatures, (namely) Ashvasena, Maya and the four Sharangakas (a kind of feathery creatures).
